prompt: Sudden frost left the hungry ducks with (little) open water than before.
explanation_ru: Water — неисчисляемое существительное, поэтому для сравнения «меньше» используется less, а не fewer.

prompt: With the new bike pass, our racks fill (early) than before.
explanation_ru: После глагола fill нужно наречие в сравнительной степени: у early конечная -y меняется на -ier (earlier).

prompt: Amina: Do we have (many) carrots as we need for eight guests?
explanation_ru: Перед союзом as с исчисляемым существительным carrots используется конструкция as many… as («столько же…, сколько»).

prompt: Five rainy school days left our family with (few) dry socks than usual.
explanation_ru: Socks — исчисляемое существительное во множественном числе, поэтому для «меньше» требуется fewer.

prompt: Our cabin box doesn't hold (much) dry wood as we expected.
explanation_ru: С неисчисляемым существительным wood перед as используется конструкция (not) as much… as (в отрицании допустимо so much).

prompt: Weekend bakery jobs fill (fast) in spring than in cold winter months.
explanation_ru: Fast — короткое наречие без суффикса -ly, поэтому его сравнительная степень образуется с -er: faster.

prompt: Neighbours, please watch out: fake parcel messages arrive (frequently) before the winter holidays.
explanation_ru: Длинные наречия на -ly образуют сравнительную степень при помощи more: more frequently.

prompt: The jazz band played (loudly) than I expected, so we had (little) space to talk.
explanation_ru: Наречие loudly образует сравнительную степень more loudly (в разговорной речи также louder), а с неисчисляемым space нужно less.

prompt: Do adults who keep their phones beside the bed sleep (badly) than people who switch them off?
explanation_ru: Наречие badly имеет неправильную сравнительную степень worse (формы more badly не существует).

prompt: Heavy rain turned the dig into mud, and we have (few) clean brushes than we ordered.
explanation_ru: С исчисляемым существительным brushes во множественном числе используется fewer, а не less.

prompt: Weekend beginners in Lola's art class pick bright green paint (often) than pale colours.
explanation_ru: Наречие частотности often образует сравнительную степень с помощью more: more often.

prompt: Walking pupils reach the village school gate (safely) than before thanks to the new crossing.
explanation_ru: Глагол reach описывается наречием safely; его сравнительная степень строится через more: more safely.

prompt: Why do my overseas book parcels arrive (slowly) this autumn, while the boxes look thinner?
explanation_ru: Наречие на -ly образует сравнительную степень с more (more slowly); в неформальной речи встречается и slower.

prompt: Although the solar sea sensors are smaller than the heavy old cables, they report tide heights (reliably) during winter storms.
explanation_ru: Действие глагола report характеризуется наречием reliably, сравнительная степень которого — more reliably.

prompt: Cooking warm oats before morning lectures isn't hard, and it helps me listen (well) and work (steadily) until lunch.
explanation_ru: Неправильное наречие well меняется на better (не more good), а наречие на -ly steadily требует more steadily.

prompt: Because the city replaced the bumpy bricks with smooth paths, my bike rolls (gently) on rainy mornings than it used to.
explanation_ru: Глагол rolls требует наречия образа действия в сравнительной степени — more gently.

prompt: Urska noticed that pale morning fog stays (long) over the cold lake in November and doesn't clear (quickly) as it does in July.
explanation_ru: Короткое наречие long образует форму longer, а в отрицательном сравнении с as используется not as quickly as.

prompt: Our town choir meets on Thursdays in the hall. After slow warm-ups, we sing (well) than in autumn. We don't shout, and everyone listens (carefully) than before.
explanation_ru: После глаголов sing и listen нужны наречия: well имеет неправильную форму better, а carefully образует more carefully.

prompt: Spiros loves baking lemon biscuits in his sunny kitchen. He puts the mix in the fridge before he rolls it. Then the biscuits bake (lightly) and keep their shape (long) than before.
explanation_ru: Наречие на -ly lightly принимает more (more lightly), а короткое наречие long образует форму на -er (longer).

prompt: Strong winds delayed four afternoon flights at our small airport. The staff don't have (many) chairs as there are passengers waiting here. Nobody seems to have (much) patience as they did at noon, either! Can't the wind drop a bit (soon)?
explanation_ru: С исчисляемым chairs перед as нужно as many, с неисчисляемым patience — as much, а короткое наречие soon даёт sooner.

prompt: I started practising slow turns at the local pool on Tuesdays. At first my coach shook his head because I rushed every wall. Since I slowed down, I breathe (calmly), push off (hard), and finish each lap (fast) than in winter.
explanation_ru: Наречие calmly требует more calmly, а короткие наречия hard и fast образуют формы на -er: harder (не hardlier) и faster.

prompt: Your spotted puppy arrived at the rescue centre looking very shy. After three quiet weeks, he walks (happily) on his lead than on day one. He also runs (far) across the grass before coming back to nap on my warm slippers.
explanation_ru: Наречие на -ly happily образует форму more happily, а неправильное наречие far — further или farther.

prompt: Irene checked our studio page to see what local readers enjoy. Short voice videos travel (far) across town than long photo albums ever did. Viewers reply (quickly) in the comments, too, and ask smart questions.
explanation_ru: Наречие far имеет неправильную сравнительную степень further/farther, а наречие quickly образует форму more quickly.

prompt: When our furniture office introduced flexible Fridays, some managers feared results would go (badly) than usual. Instead, staff work (hard) from Monday to Thursday and plan meetings (carefully) than before. Almost nobody calls in sick anymore.
explanation_ru: Неправильное наречие badly меняется на worse, короткое hard — на harder, а длинное carefully — на more carefully.

prompt: Locking our back garden alleys together took one short meeting with the neighbours. Although we didn't buy cameras, thieves can't reach our sheds (easily) as they did in winter. Everyone checks the side gates (closely) than before, and the street feels safe.
explanation_ru: В отрицательном сравнении с as используется (not) as easily as, а перед than наречие closely принимает more: more closely.

prompt: I met Callum at Brisbane Airport after a year apart, and I almost didn't recognise him. Does a teenager really grow that much? He carries heavy suitcases (easily) than his dad, though he doesn't pack (neatly) as he used to. At least he still bends down to give me a huge hug.
explanation_ru: С than наречие easily образует форму more easily, а в отрицательном сравнении с as требуется as neatly.

prompt: Sorry, the print shop sent ___ song booklets than we ordered.
explanation_ru: Booklets — исчисляемое существительное во множественном числе, поэтому нужно fewer; частая ошибка — ставить less.

prompt: After the sharpener broke, our table has ___ sharp pencils than yours.
explanation_ru: Перед исчисляемым существительным pencils в сравнении с than употребляется fewer, а не less.

prompt: These olive oil bottles look the same height, yet they hold ___ oil than last winter.
explanation_ru: Oil — неисчисляемое существительное, поэтому для значения «меньше» используется less, а не fewer.

prompt: Strong harbour winds gave our rowing teams ___ calm mornings to practise than we planned.
explanation_ru: Mornings — исчисляемое существительное, поэтому верно fewer; типичная ошибка — использовать less или not much.

prompt: Light winter snow meant the valley canals do not carry ___ cool water as the grape farms need.
explanation_ru: С неисчисляемым существительным water в конструкции not… as используется as much; as many подходит только для исчисляемых.

prompt: Bright new roadside lamps shine all night, so local star watchers get ___ dark hours to spot shooting stars than before.
explanation_ru: Hours — исчисляемое существительное, поэтому нужно far fewer; типичные ошибки — ставить less или добавлять лишнее more.

prompt: A dry winter left the ducks with fewer rainwater than before.
answer: A dry winter left the ducks with less rainwater than before.
accepted_answers: A dry winter left the ducks with less rainwater than before.
explanation_ru: Rainwater — неисчисляемое существительное, поэтому вместо fewer нужно less.

prompt: Drivers find less free spaces on the top deck after eight.
answer: Drivers find fewer free spaces on the top deck after eight.
accepted_answers: Drivers find fewer free spaces on the top deck after eight.
explanation_ru: Spaces — исчисляемое существительное во множественном числе, поэтому правильно fewer, а не less.

prompt: Warm July evenings bring far more film fans to the square than chilly spring nights do.
answer: Warm July evenings bring far more film fans to the square than chilly spring nights do.
accepted_answers: Warm July evenings bring far more film fans to the square than chilly spring nights do.
explanation_ru: Ошибки нет: far more film fans… than… do грамматически верно сочетает усилитель far с more и исчисляемым существительным.

prompt: Workers who take a real lunch break feel rested and work more good in the afternoon.
answer: Workers who take a real lunch break feel rested and work better in the afternoon.
accepted_answers: Workers who take a real lunch break feel rested and work better in the afternoon.
explanation_ru: После глагола work нужно наречие well в сравнительной степени — better; форма more good является ошибкой.

prompt: This weather app runs slower than my old one, and my phone battery works hardlier just to load giant moving adverts.
answer: This weather app runs slower than my old one, and my phone battery works harder just to load giant moving adverts.
accepted_answers: This weather app runs slower than my old one, and my phone battery works harder just to load giant moving adverts.
explanation_ru: Наречие «усерднее / с большей нагрузкой» — harder; формы hardlier не существует, а hardly означает «едва».

prompt: Extra relatives arrived early for the wedding dinner, so Catarina ran short of folding chairs. Which message makes sense?
options: We have as many chairs as guests, so nobody needs to stand.
We have fewer chairs than guests, so please bring ten more from the store.
We have less chairs than guests, so please bring ten more from the store.
We have more chairs than guests, so put the extra ones back outside.
explanation_ru: Стульев не хватает, а chairs — исчисляемое существительное, поэтому грамматически и по смыслу подходит только fewer chairs than guests.

prompt: Manolo warned his neighbours that scam bank messages arrive much more often during busy summer holidays than in quiet months. Which sentence matches his warning?
options: Scam texts arrive as rarely in July as they do during quiet winter weeks.
Neighbours receive fewer fake bank texts during the summer break than in winter.
Fake bank messages land far more frequently in summer than during quiet months.
Residents get less fake bank alerts in summer because scammers go on holiday.
explanation_ru: Третий вариант верно передаёт смысл предупреждения и правильно строит сравнительную степень наречия: far more frequently.

prompt: Toby put a funny sign on the print-room cupboard because blue pens keep disappearing and staff can barely find one to sign forms. Which sign fits?
options: We have fewer blue pens left in this cupboard than we have delivery slips to sign.
We have less blue pens left in this cupboard than we have delivery slips to sign.
Blue pens disappear more slowly this week, so everyone can take three home.
There are as many blue pens on the shelf as we need for the whole year.
explanation_ru: Ручек меньше, чем бланков, и pens — исчисляемое существительное, поэтому верна только форма fewer blue pens.

prompt: We don't have as many clean trainers as we had on Monday. → We have …
answer: We have fewer clean trainers than we had on Monday.
accepted_answers: We have fewer clean trainers than we had on Monday.
We have fewer clean trainers than on Monday.
explanation_ru: Отрицательное сравнение not as many + исчисляемое существительное перефразируется с помощью fewer… than.

prompt: The crowded pancake porch has less space between tables than our local cafe. → The crowded pancake porch doesn't have …
answer: The crowded pancake porch doesn't have as much space between tables as our local cafe.
accepted_answers: The crowded pancake porch doesn't have as much space between tables as our local cafe.
The crowded pancake porch doesn't have so much space between tables as our local cafe.
explanation_ru: Сравнение less + неисчисляемое существительное (space) перестраивается в конструкцию doesn't have as much… as.
